```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150, fig.width = 7
)
```

Every plot that `autoplot()` draws, using `png_ants`: real ant bait data
from the Mt Wilhelm elevational gradient, Papua New Guinea. Each entry has three tabs: the plot, the tidy table behind it, and
the code. All plots use the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette and
`theme_tidydiversity()` by default; see the
[publication figures](publication.html) article for customisation.

Maps are in the companion package tidymapr; see its
[Gallery](https://gitlab.com/jimmy.moses/tidymapr/-/blob/main/vignettes/articles/gallery.Rmd).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
wet <- filter(png_ants, season == "wet")
```

## Rarefaction and extrapolation by sample size {.tabset}

```{r rarefy-data, include = FALSE}

```

### Plot

```{r rarefy, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Rarefaction and extrapolation by sample size"}
autoplot(curves)
```

### Table

```{r rarefy-table}
curves
```

### Code


## Coverage-standardised beta diversity {.tabset}


### Plot


### Table

```{r hill-beta-table}

```

### Code

```r

autoplot(hb)
```

## Ordination triplot {.tabset}

An RDA of the Wanang butterflies constrained by year and month: sites,
the ten best-fitting species (red arrows), the month gradient (dark arrow),
year centroids and
ellipses for each year.

```{r triplot-data, include = FALSE}
butterflies <- mutate(wanang_butterflies, year = factor(paste("Year", year)))
rda <- ord_fit(butterflies, method = "rda", formula = ~ year + month)
```

### Plot

```{r triplot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "RDA triplot of Wanang butterfly sampling days coloured by year, with species arrows, year and month centroids and year ellipses"}
autoplot(rda, colour = year, ellipse = "sd", species = 10)
```

### Code

```r
butterflies <- mutate(wanang_butterflies, year = factor(paste("Year", year)))
rda <- ord_fit(butterflies, method = "rda", formula = ~ year + month)
autoplot(rda, colour = year, ellipse = "sd", species = 10)
```

## Shared species: Venn diagram {.tabset}

`plot_venn()` counts the species found in each combination of two to four
groups. Here, ant species at four elevations on Mt Wilhelm.

### Plot

```{r venn, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Venn diagram of ant species shared between 200, 700, 1200 and 1700 m on Mt Wilhelm"}
plot_venn(filter(png_ants, elevation %in% c(200, 700, 1200, 1700)), group = elevation)
```

### Two groups

```{r venn-2, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Venn diagram of caterpillar morphospecies shared between primary and secondary forest at Wanang"}
plot_venn(wanang_caterpillars, group = site)
```

### Code

```r
plot_venn(filter(png_ants, elevation %in% c(200, 700, 1200, 1700)), group = elevation)
plot_venn(wanang_caterpillars, group = site)
```

## Phylogenetic diversity {.tabset}

`plot_phylo()` draws the tree with each species' relative abundance per
site. The coloured branches lead to the frogs found at 200 m: their total
length is Faith's PD for that site. The tree here is a taxonomic tree
(family, genus, species) with Grafen branch lengths; use a dated
phylogeny where one exists.

```{r phylo-data, include = FALSE}
frogs <- mutate(png_frogs,
  genus = sub(" .*", "", scientific_name),
  tip = gsub(" ", "_", scientific_name)
)
tax <- distinct(as.data.frame(frogs[c("family", "genus", "tip")]))
tax[] <- lapply(tax, factor)
tree <- ape::compute.brlen(ape::as.phylo(~ family / genus / tip, data = tax))
```

### Plot

```{r phylo, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 9, fig.alt = "Phylogram of Mt Wilhelm frogs with dots for relative abundance at each elevation and the branches present at 200 m highlighted"}
plot_phylo(tree, frogs, species = tip, abundance = abundance, highlight = "MW0200")
```

### Code

```r
frogs <- mutate(png_frogs,
  genus = sub(" .*", "", scientific_name),
  tip = gsub(" ", "_", scientific_name)
)
tax <- distinct(as.data.frame(frogs[c("family", "genus", "tip")]))
tax[] <- lapply(tax, factor)
tree <- ape::compute.brlen(ape::as.phylo(~ family / genus / tip, data = tax))
plot_phylo(tree, frogs, species = tip, abundance = abundance, highlight = "MW0200")
```

## Functional trait space {.tabset}

`plot_trait_space()` places the alpine plants of the `aravo` data in a
PCoA of Gower trait distances. Each hull encloses the species found under
one level of zoogenic disturbance (its area is the two-dimensional
functional richness) and the diamonds are cover-weighted mean positions.

### Plot

```{r trait-space, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5.5, fig.alt = "Functional trait space of alpine plants with convex hulls and weighted mean positions for three levels of zoogenic disturbance"}
aravo <- data_aravo()
plot_trait_space(aravo$traits, aravo$community, group = ZoogD, abundance = cover)
```

### Code

```r
aravo <- data_aravo()
plot_trait_space(aravo$traits, aravo$community, group = ZoogD, abundance = cover)
```

## Maps

Maps are drawn by the companion package
[tidymapr](https://gitlab.com/jimmy.moses/tidymapr), which takes the same tidy
tables. Its [Gallery](https://gitlab.com/jimmy.moses/tidymapr/-/blob/main/vignettes/articles/gallery.Rmd)
shows study-site, Hill-number, elevation and species distribution maps
from real, published records.
